logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, Site Administration’s configuration list uses the wrong capitalization for the supported IntelliJ IDEA editor: it displays “Intellij IDEA.” This is a visible product-name spelling error, not a failure to open the editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DefaultOpenWithEditorApps hardcodes Intellij IDEA.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, Site Administration’s configuration list uses the wrong capitalization for the supported IntelliJ IDEA editor: it displays “Intellij IDEA.” This is a visible product-name spelling error, not a failure to open the editor.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration’s Cron Tasks list, the archive-cleanup task description ends with “etc..” instead of a single full stop. The defect is the duplicated punctuation in the task label; the report does not establish that cleanup itself fails.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The English locale literal ends etc..
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration’s Cron Tasks list, the archive-cleanup task description ends with “etc..” instead of a single full stop. The defect is the duplicated punctuation in the task label; the report does not establish that cleanup itself fails.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Repositories, choosing Alphabetically sorts repositories by their owner before their own name. A repository whose name belongs near the beginning can therefore appear after later-named repositories belonging to another owner, instead of one alphabetical list by repository name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The alpha repository ordering sorts owner_name before lower_name, grouping repositories by owner even when inventory presents a name sort.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Repositories, choose Alphabetically with repositories belonging to both a user and an organization. A repository with an alphabetically earlier name can appear after later-named repositories because the list groups by owner before comparing repository names.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, an administrator can customize the Open with editor links using name-to-URL mappings. Saving a nonempty entry without the required equals-sign delimiter reports no validation error but removes the entry and leaves the field blank, so an invalid edit silently erases the override instead of remaining available for correction.
logicalBugs.rootCause: marshalOpenWithApps continues past lines without = or nonempty name/URL and returns successful JSON rather than a validation error.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, an administrator can customize the Open with editor links using name-to-URL mappings. Saving a nonempty entry without the required equals-sign delimiter reports no validation error but removes the entry and leaves the field blank, so an invalid edit silently erases the override instead of remaining available for correction.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a phone-width Site Administration > Monitor page, the diagnosis-report controls overlap the Stacktrace tab. The page also extends beyond the viewport, allowing horizontal scrolling that moves process controls out of view instead of keeping the monitoring interface within the screen.
logicalBugs.rootCause: trace_tabs places the compact tab menu and diagnosis form on one flex row without responsive wrapping; intrinsic widths force overlap and widen the document.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a phone-width Site Administration > Monitor page, the diagnosis-report controls overlap the Stacktrace tab. The page also extends beyond the viewport, allowing horizontal scrolling that moves process controls out of view instead of keeping the monitoring interface within the screen.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at 390px, Site Administration inventory action buttons cover their headings’ totals. New Organization, Create User Account and Unadopted Repositories can overlap the corresponding "Total: N" text rather than stacking beside/below it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Admin list templates put their action inside .ui.attached.header > .ui.right. The shared header CSS positions that action absolutely at the right edge without reserving space in the heading or stacking it at narrow widths, so heading text can run beneath the button.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, at a 390px width, the New Organization button covers part of the organization-total heading.

In Gitea, sign in as a site administrator and open User Accounts at a 390px-wide viewport. Create User Account covers the end of User Account Management (Total: N), hiding the total even when a search reduces it to one. At 480px and wider the heading fits, and the button still opens the account-creation form.

In Gitea, sign in as a site administrator and open Site Administration > Repositories at a 390px-wide viewport. Unadopted Repositories covers the Total: N portion of the Repository Management heading, including for a filtered total of one. At 480px and wider the heading fits, and the button still opens Unadopted Repositories.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after an administrator deletes the sole repository matching an inventory search and Public filter, the redirect drops both query parameters, clears the search, and displays unrelated repositories instead of the now-empty filtered results.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DeleteRepository reconstructs the redirect using only page and sort, omitting q, private and the other filter parameters.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after an administrator deletes the sole repository matching an inventory search and Public filter, the redirect drops both query parameters, clears the search, and displays unrelated repositories instead of the now-empty filtered results.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when an administrator deletes the only repository on the last page of Site Administration → Repositories, the redirect returns to that now out-of-range page, which shows the total count but "No results found." and no pagination controls.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Deletion preserves the requested page; the subsequent list queries its offset before pagination can adjust it, leaving an empty page after the last row is deleted.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when an administrator deletes the only repository on the last page of Site Administration → Repositories, the redirect returns to that now out-of-range page, which shows the total count but "No results found." and no pagination controls.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea organization’s public profile at phone width, the Follow or Unfollow button is squeezed beside the organization name. Its short label breaks in the middle of words and can span several lines, rather than remaining a readable action button.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The organization name and action group share a header row within a flex column; the following control lacks its own minimum width/nowrap sizing when the header consumes phone width.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea organization’s public profile at phone width, the Follow or Unfollow button is squeezed beside the organization name. Its short label breaks in the middle of words and can span several lines, rather than remaining a readable action button.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in organization settings, emptying the Contact Email field and clicking Update Settings shows 'Organization settings have been updated.', but the old address is kept in the form and the organization header.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsPost calls ReplacePrimaryEmailAddress only for nonempty Email and omits an update when it is cleared.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in organization settings, emptying the Contact Email field and clicking Update Settings shows 'Organization settings have been updated.', but the old address is kept in the form and the organization header.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Edit User, a blank or invalid/out-of-range Maximum Number of Repositories reports a successful save but replaces the previous limit with 0. That zero can block repository creation instead of rejecting the input or using the documented -1 default.
logicalBugs.rootCause: EditUserForm uses a plain int field without a required or lexical/range validator; failed/empty binding produces zero, and the handler persists form.MaxRepoCreation as an explicit update.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Edit User, clearing the Maximum Number of Repositories field and saving reports success but stores 0, which blocks the user from creating any repositories, instead of rejecting the blank value or using the default (-1).

On Gitea’s Site Administration > Edit User Account, entering a Maximum Number of Repositories that's too large (or not a plain number, such as 1e3) shows "The user account has been updated" but saves the limit as 0, erasing the previous value and blocking the user from creating repositories.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, submitting organization settings with a name already taken or reserved shows a rename error but replaces other pending text/settings with saved values. It can also uncheck Repository admin can add and remove access for teams, so correcting the name and saving silently disables that previously enabled option.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The rejection path renders tplSettingsOptions while its inputs read the persisted organization. RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess is populated by GET but not the error path, so the checkbox also loses its value.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in organization settings, submitting a name that's already taken or reserved shows the right error, but the form is redrawn from the saved values, so the other edits from the same submission (full name, description, website, location, visibility, repository limit) are lost.

In Gitea, when saving an organization's settings is rejected (for example a name that's already taken), the form reloads with the error, but the previously checked 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' option is unchecked. Fixing the error and saving again turns that permission off without the user noticing.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues, entering a maximum worker count below -1 (such as -2) reports Settings Updated and stores -1 instead. The form gives no validation message or sign that the entered value was rejected or changed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateQueue explicitly converts maxNumber < -1 to -1 and still flashes settings changed.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues, entering a maximum worker count below -1 (such as -2) reports Settings Updated and stores -1 instead. The form gives no validation message or sign that the entered value was rejected or changed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitor, confirming Cancel on a running diagnosis report process reports success, but the process keeps running for its full duration and the browser still downloads the report afterwards. The diagnosis handler waits out its full time without checking for cancellation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The handler sleeps for the sampling duration without selecting on the process context cancellation, then completes the response.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitor, confirming Cancel on a running diagnosis report process reports success, but the process keeps running for its full duration and the browser still downloads the report afterwards. The diagnosis handler waits out its full time without checking for cancellation.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Site Administration User Accounts, Organizations and User Emails, choosing a sort and then submitting a search/filter drops that sort. The results return in the page’s default ordering rather than narrowing the selected order.
logicalBugs.rootCause: User, organization and email search forms do not carry the current sort as a hidden input. Sort buttons contribute a value only when clicked, so other submissions drop it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > User Accounts, choosing a sort and then searching or applying a filter reloads the list in alphabetical order, dropping the selected sort.
In Gitea’s Site Administration > Organizations, choosing a sort and then searching reloads the list in alphabetical order, dropping the selected sort.
In Gitea’s Site Administration > User Emails, choosing a sort (such as reverse username) and then searching returns results in the default ascending email order and drops the sort from the URL.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, browser Back can restore earlier repository results/URL while leaving later search or filter controls in place. On Explore, changing Sort after Back can silently reapply an undone Public/private filter; in admin repository inventory, the search box can keep the later unmatched query above the earlier results.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The change handler builds navigation from FormData of the restored form without synchronizing controls from the current URL on pageshow/popstate. Browser history can restore results independently of control values.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Repositories, search for a matching repository, submit a different query with no matches, then use browser Back. The earlier matching rows return, but the search field still shows the later nonmatching query instead of the query represented by the results.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration > User Accounts, submit one search that finds users, then another that finds none, and use browser Back. The earlier matching user rows return, but the search field still contains the later nonmatching query, so the visible query does not describe the displayed results.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The server-rendered user search input has browser-restorable value state with no URL synchronization on history restoration, so later input can appear above earlier results.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > User Accounts, submit a search that matches users, follow it with a query that matches none, then use browser Back. The matching users return while the input retains the nonmatching query, leaving the visible search text inconsistent with the rows.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, setting a queue's Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) is accepted with "Settings Updated", but the queue still starts a worker when work arrives, and nothing explains that 0 doesn't stop it. The setting looks like it caps workers at zero but has no such effect.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The workergroup start condition explicitly permits noWorker && workerMaxNum <= 0; the admin numeric setting does not communicate these special semantics.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, setting a queue's Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) is accepted with "Settings Updated", but the queue still starts a worker when work arrives, and nothing explains that 0 doesn't stop it. The setting looks like it caps workers at zero but has no such effect.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea organization's settings, clearing Maximum Number of Repositories and saving stores a limit of 0, which blocks the organization from creating repositories, instead of falling back to the default (-1, use the global limit) when the field is unset.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateOrgSettingForm represents MaxRepoCreation as a plain int; blank binding is zero and SettingsPost persists it rather than interpreting missing input as the default.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea organization's settings, clearing Maximum Number of Repositories and saving stores a limit of 0, which blocks the organization from creating repositories, instead of falling back to the default (-1, use the global limit) when the field is unset.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after opening Cancel process at desktop width and resizing to 390 pixels, the dialog moves beyond the right and bottom edges. Dismissing with Escape and reopening at the mobile width still shows a clipped dialog with Confirm outside the viewport.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The stacktrace layout can exceed viewport width and the generic modal is opened through link-action using document/dimmer geometry rather than constraining this overflowing monitor layout.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after opening Cancel process at desktop width and resizing to 390 pixels, the dialog moves beyond the right and bottom edges. Dismissing with Escape and reopening at the mobile width still shows a clipped dialog with Confirm outside the viewport.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s Site Administration has a user page with User Details and User Emails panels. At phone widths, a user with a short email can leave both panels side by side, squeezing the details into a roughly 100–140px column whose labels and values break mid-word and become very tall. A long email can make the panels stack but leave the Primary or Activated badges clipped. These are layout failures on the individual user page, distinct from action buttons covering totals on the account list.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The admin user page uses wrapping flex columns whose stacking depends on their minimum content widths rather than a phone-width breakpoint. The details list permits a nearly zero minimum width and breaks text anywhere, so that column can shrink instead of moving below the email panel. Email status labels are also shrinkable and nonwrapping, which can clip their text even when the columns stack.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, as a site administrator, create a user with a short email address. At a 390px-wide viewport, open that user from Site Administration > User Accounts. User Details stays beside User Emails in a very narrow column; labels such as Authentication and Restricted break mid-word and the panel becomes unusually tall. The seeded users can stack normally, so use a fresh short-email account.

On Gitea’s individual user page in Site Administration, use an account with a long email address at phone width. The User Details and User Emails panels can stack, but status badges such as Primary or Activated in the email panel are cut off instead of displaying their complete labels.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace initially displays a Goroutines count, meaning the number of running lightweight execution tasks, but no trace list and no explanation of how to display one. Neither Running Processes nor Stacktrace appears selected. Choosing one loads the diagnostic details. The missing guidance is the accepted defect; the deliberate decision not to collect traces on the initial page is not itself a failed load.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Stacktrace deliberately avoids loading process data until a show parameter is supplied, keeping the diagnostic entry page usable under server stress. The template displays the count without an empty-state instruction, and the tab bar marks neither diagnostic view active, leaving the administrator uninformed about the required next action.
reproductionPaths: As a Gitea site administrator, open Monitoring > Trace from the sidebar. The page shows a Goroutines count with no list and no hint that Running Processes or Stacktrace must be chosen. Click Running Processes to see the available diagnostic list; the problem is the unexplained initial view, not a claim that those tabs fail.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s diagnosis report downloads a ZIP containing a timed performance profile. Entering zero, a negative number, blank text or nonnumeric text in its duration field silently produces an approximately one-second report without validation or notice that the value was corrected. The intended minimum in this version is one second; a demand for a five-second minimum is a different, rejected expectation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: MonitorDiagnosis parses seconds as an integer, yielding zero for blank or invalid input, and clamps values at or below one to one without reporting a correction. The plain text field provides no range hint or validation. The one-second floor is intentional; the missing explanation for silently coerced input is the defect.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Site Administration > Monitoring > Stacktrace, enter 0, a negative value, blank text or abc as the Download diagnosis report duration. Download it and observe an approximately one-second ZIP response with no correction message or allowed-range hint. Match complaints about missing feedback, rather than assertions that valid 1- or 3-second requests must last at least five seconds.

logicalBugs.description: In production mode, Gitea deliberately hides Performance Trace from the administrator’s Monitoring > Trace tabs. Its direct address still serves the page of HTTP and database timings, with no active tab and no navigation entry leading there. The accepted inconsistency is serving a page whose navigation is intentionally hidden, not unauthorized access by an ordinary user or a claim that merely hiding the tab is wrong.
logicalBugs.rootCause: monitorTraceCommon disables ShowAdminPerformanceTraceTab in production and the tab template obeys it. The performance-trace route is registered unconditionally and PerfTrace does not check that production visibility condition, so it serves records while selecting a tab that was never rendered.
reproductionPaths: As a Gitea site administrator in production mode, open Monitoring > Trace and see only Running Processes and Stacktrace. Open /-/admin/monitor/perftrace directly: performance trace records render, but the tab bar has no Performance Trace entry and no active tab. Reports of this page being reachable only by a typed address or lacking its navigation entry match this inconsistency.
